linkedin_posts: Earnalism's first Bengali audiobook is live: দুই বিঘা জমি by রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর. The important product decision was not speed; it was release truth. We waited for source verification, listening QA, measured paragraph/stanza sync, metadata, endpoint, and browser gates.

Bengali typography and narration deserve the same product rigor as English classics. Earnalism now has an approved Bengali audiobook live, but we still label the experience honestly as section-following narration, not word-level sync.
Our launch principle: reader editions can be live before audio, but audio never appears until it passes gates. দুই বিঘা জমি is the first Bengali proof point.

linkedin_posts: A Ghost Story is part of Earnalism's live audiobook shelf because it is short, marketable, and asset-backed. It also shows why short classics are better first paid tests than long prestige titles.
For launch, we are separating reader-first authority from audiobook conversion. A Ghost Story is a good conversion candidate; Dracula stays a long-form reader/SEO anchor until audio QA is safe.
Earnalism's first English audio marketing should start with stories that can prove completion, listening quality, and conversion quickly. A Ghost Story fits that role.
